resources.string: No keys yet: choose the prod.keys from your own Switch
This file has no header_key; choose a valid prod.keys
Choose keys, XCI and output folder first
Extract XCI, NSP and NSZ to ExeFS and RomFS

• A dump of a game you own: an .xci, .nsp or .nsz file.
• Your own prod.keys, dumped from your own Switch (for example with Lockpick_RCM).
• For NSP and NSZ the app takes the title key from the tickets (.tik) inside the file. If there is none, add the title key as a line in your keys file (title.keys format).

The app ships no keys or game files.

1. Choose your prod.keys. You only do this once: the app remembers them.
2. Choose your dump (XCI, NSP or NSZ).
3. Choose the folder for the result.
4. Switch ExeFS and/or RomFS on and tap Extract.

While extracting you see progress, speed and time left. Tap Cancel to stop.

The files go into a new folder named after your dump + _extracted:

MyGame_extracted/
 0100…/exefs/ main, main.npdm, …
 0100…/romfs/ the game data

The 0100… folder is the game’s title ID. Copy that folder to your PC or recomp project afterwards.

• Make sure you have enough free space: RomFS is often several GB.
• Keep the app open while extracting; the screen stays on.
• An NSZ is compressed and takes a bit more processing time.
• Updates and DLC (patches) are not supported: pick the base game.

• "header_key" or "NCA header could not be decrypted": your prod.keys do not match this dump or are incomplete.
• "master_key_xx is missing": your keys come from older firmware than the game needs. Dump new keys.
• "title key … not in your key file": for an NSP/NSZ without a ticket, add the title key.
• "truncated": the file was not copied completely.

Tap the question mark at the top right to see this guide again.

A Switch game (XCI, NSP or NSZ) is one big encrypted package. A recomp tool cannot use it as is.

This app opens that package with the keys from your own Switch and unpacks it into ordinary folders and files: ExeFS (the game’s code) and RomFS (the game data).

That is the first step of a recomp. Static recompilation translates a game’s code into a program that runs on another device without an emulator, and these are exactly the files it needs.

Everything happens on your phone; nothing is uploaded.
Your dump is decrypted with your keys and unpacked into ExeFS and RomFS

ExeFS: the code
• main: the game program itself. This is what a recompiler translates.
• main.npdm: information about the program (including the title ID and permissions).
• rtld, sdk, subsdk…: libraries the game ships with.
These files stay in the NSO format used on the Switch; the app does not unpack them further.

RomFS: the game data
• Images, models, sound, music, levels and text.
• Often thousands of files and several GB.

Only need the code? Switch RomFS off: it saves a lot of time and space.
ExeFS is the game’s code (needed for a recomp). RomFS is the game data such as images and sound, often several GB.
